html:
A composer and singer of south India who lived from 1767 to 1847. He is the best loved of the "trinity" of Carnatic music, the classical music of the south, with his contemporaries Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri.

He lived most of his life at Tiruvaiyaru, on the Kaveri river near Thanjavur, then ruled by Maratha kings. He was a devotee of the god Rama and refused, by tradition, an invitation to sing for the king, choosing devotion over a court post. He lived simply, singing his songs in the streets and at home.

He composed hundreds of songs, called kritis, mostly in Telugu, the language of much south Indian court music. They are prayers, pleas and conversations with Rama, set in many ragas. The kriti form he perfected, with its opening theme and sections for improvised variation, is still the core of the Carnatic concert.

Every January musicians gather at his tomb at Tiruvaiyaru for the Tyagaraja Aradhana festival and sing his five great Pancharatna kritis together. His devotion places him in the long line of the bhakti movement.
